section_summaries.individual_presentation: several months of low back pain, progressive stiffness of the abdominal, low back, and thigh muscles, increased lumbar lordosis, focal hyperhidrosis at different sites episodic pain and stiffness of his lumbar musculature marked stiffness of the lower back and abdominal muscles as well as the proximal muscles of the lower extremities; severe episodic spasms especially in lumbar area triggered by physical activity; 20-lb weight gain; progressive curvature of lumbar spine; hyperhidrosis; muscular with hypertrophied lumbar, thigh, and calf musculature; hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: Electromyography showed continuous activity of the paraspinal and thigh muscles, serum and cerebrospinal fluid antibodies to glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) were markedly elevated initially diagnosed as having degenerative arthritis CSF analysis demonstrated a protein of 25 mg/dl, glucose of 76 mg/dl, cell count of 2 WBC and no RBC, and a differential of 100% mononuclear cells; laboratory studies including hemogram, electrolytes, liver enzymes, urinalysis, thyroid function panel, coagulation studies, glucose tolerance test, ANA, ACTH stimulation test, and erythrocyte sedimentation tests were all normal; tests for HLA-B27, VDRL, HIV and Lyme titer were negative; pulmonary function tests showed FVC of 3.93 L (86%), FEV1 of 3.12 L (83%), and a ratio of 79%
section_summaries.individual_treatment: Diazepam and Lioresal offered partial pain relief Combination of diazepam and Lioresal, at a dosage of 15 mg of each daily injected a total of 560 U of botulinum toxin type A into the lumbar paraspinal muscles over a period of 3 weeks at three different injecting sessions (160, 200, and 200 U)
section_summaries.individual_outcome: produced some symptomatic pain relief A week after the last injection, the patient reported almost total relief from exertional pain and complete cessation of spontaneous painful spasms The patient sustained this degree of clinical improvement over a month of follow-up
section_summaries.individual_limitations: no abnormalities in cranial nerves and cerebellar and sensory systems; no involuntary movements noted initial dose of 560 U exceeds the total dose recommended for dystonia (400-450 U for torticollis), and repeated injection of such a dose may produce antibodies to botulinum toxin
